passage: A great deal of Baroque music was never fully written out. In place of a complete keyboard part, composers often supplied only a bass line marked with small numbers—a figured bass—indicating which chords to build above each note. The player was expected to realize this shorthand in performance, choosing how to space the chords, when to add ornaments, and how full or sparse the texture should be from moment to moment. Two skilled performers working from the same figured bass could therefore produce noticeably different accompaniments, both of them correct. For modern players trained to reproduce a score exactly, this is an unfamiliar freedom; for Baroque musicians, improvising within the rules of the figured bass was simply part of what it meant to know the music.
question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It argues that modern performers play Baroque music far more accurately than the composers' own contemporaries ever managed to.
It explains a Baroque notational shorthand and then draws out the improvisatory freedom that performing from it required.
It traces the gradual replacement of the figured bass by fully written-out keyboard parts over the course of the eighteenth century.
It describes the mathematical system by which the numbers in a figured bass were calculated from the notes of the bass line.

explanation: The correct answer is B. The passage first explains what a figured bass is—a bass line with numbers telling the player which chords to build—and then develops the freedom that realizing it demanded, noting that two players could produce different yet equally correct accompaniments. Its structure is explanation followed by the point about performer freedom. Choice A makes an accuracy claim the passage does not support. Choice C describes a historical replacement the passage does not narrate. Choice D invents a mathematical system that the passage does not describe.

_meta.anchor: Figured bass in Baroque music; notation and improvisatory realization
